summary: In July 2026, a researcher testing Grok Build v0.2.93 captured uploads of whole Git bundles to xAI storage, including tracked files the coding agent had been told not to read and the repository’s commit history. In one test, the agent was asked only to reply “OK”; the repository bundle was still transmitted. The researcher later observed that xAI had switched off the upload server-side on the tested account. The test used canary files and fake secrets; it did not establish that xAI trained on the uploaded code or exposed a real customer’s credentials.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: The controlled capture shows authority to work with task-relevant repository content expanding into transfer of all tracked files and Git history to separate xAI storage, including material the agent had been instructed not to read. The established boundary concerns the scope of data transferred, rather than a separate finding that technical capability itself supplied permission. The canary-based test does not establish real-customer confidentiality loss downstream. The researcher’s no-file-read instruction independently restricted the tested operation. A captured repository bundle contained a file that was not to be opened, with its canary intact. This supports the tested information-access boundary finding, without claiming that fake credentials were real secrets or that all consumer repositories were confidential.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The researcher’s original wire-level analysis provides captured request and bundle evidence for version 0.2.93: tracked repository content and history reached a storage endpoint separately from model-turn traffic even when the agent did not inspect those files. The researcher reported a later server-side disablement; the scope and permanence of that change across accounts are not independently established. The official changelog supports product-version context but not the upload finding. The controlled samples used fake credentials; no real secret exposure, training use or population-wide loss is proven here. Separate probes distinguish read-driven model traffic from repository snapshots, synthetic secrets from real credentials, and observed multi-GB transfer from a completed 12 GB run. The researcher corrected an earlier process-scoped measurement and distinguished retention preferences from transmission.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The tested CLI expanded task-local repository access into a repository-wide external storage action. The controlled capture establishes a target-and-scope authority failure in that implementation; it does not by itself establish downstream misuse of the data or a quantified real-customer confidentiality harm. Later server-side disablement limits current generalisation, not the observed 0.2.93 behaviour. The retained target/scope failure is bounded to the captured implementation and task, without inferring real secret disclosure, training use or population-wide damage. Tested-account disablement is resolved recovery context rather than an affirmative fleet-wide success. Independent OECD assessment finds user-agency/scope safeguards Not aligned for the captured repository-wide transfer and repair Aligned only for the subsequently observed tested-account disablement. Model-development storage and human-subject data-consent requirements address different lifecycle/participation objects and remain audit-only. No real-secret exposure, training use or fleet-wide repair is inferred. The researcher’s no-file-read instruction independently restricted the tested operation. A captured repository bundle contained a file that was not to be opened, with its canary intact. This supports the tested information-access boundary finding, without claiming that fake credentials were real secrets or that all consumer repositories were confidential.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Permission to run a coding task in a repository does not itself cover bulk transmission of all tracked files and history. The upload path and retention setting need to be visible as distinct governed actions because an ordinary model-training opt-out did not stop the captured storage transfer in the test.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: All twelve dimensions reconsidered against the amended in-place HIM 1.1.0 minimum protected-data-access threshold. A live Grok Build 0.2.93 test transmitted complete Git bundles, including real source-code projects as well as fake canary files; the original report reconstructs accepted uploads. The decisive unresolved fact for PRV S2 is whether actual source or history in those projects was non-public confidential information. The synthetic credential values do not make real files synthetic, and absence of proved customer credential loss is not a required privacy prerequisite. Repository-size bytes are not unique affected people. Until the protected status is established, retain privacy insufficient-evidence and overall SU, without asserting no privacy harm; training, retention/deletion and impact on other users remain unproved.

The researcher's wire captures and reconstructed Git bundles prove unauthorised transfer of complete tracked repositories and history to xAI storage, including a real 298-file source-code project and a second separate real code project, as well as synthetic never-read canaries. The code files were real; only the planted credentials were fake. The current public account does not establish whether the real transmitted source code/history contained non-public confidential information rather than public or otherwise authorised code. Under the revised HIM 1.1.0 PRV S2 alternative, this confidentiality discriminator — not proof of customer credentials, later misuse or a precise victim count — remains required before assigning the minimum band. Real repository transfer is positively established, protected-information status is insufficient-evidence, and later server disablement does not prove deletion.

The bounded technical task has no source-supported intimate-role claim or loss of valued human relationships, caregiving, independent relational choice or viable disengagement. Agent collaboration and persistent service continuity do not themselves establish relational substitution.

harm_impact_assessment.assessment_gap: Completed repository-scale transmission is proven in controlled tests involving real source code, but the published artefacts do not establish that the source files or history were confidential non-public information. This missing discriminator prevents a confirmed protected-data PRV S2 outcome; no S3–S5 consequence is inferred from transfer volume or fake canary credentials.

aggregate_harm_screening.rationale: A live consumer Grok Build version was tested and the researcher demonstrated concrete repository egress from their own actual local projects. This is a bounded actual egress occurrence, although protected confidential status of the specific files remains unconfirmed. The affected developer/project exposure is not a modelled collective harm cohort in any eligible Aggregate Harm dimension. No platform-wide population inference.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The repository-wide upload is unwanted behaviour directly engaging repair/override. The researcher subsequently observed server-side disablement of uploading on the tested account. That is affirmative source-bounded corrective intervention for that account; it does not establish fleet-wide deployment, permanence, removal of previously stored bundles or every data consequence.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: The separately observed server-side disablement on the tested account directly identifies appropriate repair of the unwanted upload.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The captured implementation uploaded tracked repository contents and history through a storage channel beyond the active task even when asked only to reply OK. That independently establishes failure of context-appropriate user-agency/scope safeguards in the tested workflow. The protected task boundary failed without needing a real secret leak, training use or population-wide harm; this finding is bounded to the captured client/account/version.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: The wire-level capture of task-independent repository transfer directly identifies context-appropriate human-agency/scope safeguards independently of the FC candidate.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The access-enforcement proposition requires approved logical-access authorisations to be enforced for information and system resources. The observed information operation was outside the approved boundary. With an explicit instruction not to read files, the CLI nevertheless bundled tracked repository contents and history; the researcher recovered an unread canary from that bundle. The tested read restriction was crossed. Synthetic secrets do not establish real credential exposure. This is a bounded retrospective comparison with the selected control proposition, not a claim of certification or an independently binding historical duty.
